options.name: allowextendedmastersecret
options.description: When set to C(YES), attempt to use the TLS Extended Master Secret (EMS, as described in RFC 7627) when negotiating TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 connection parameters. EMS must be supported by both the TLS client and server in order to be enabled during a handshake. This setting applies to both frontend and backend SSL profiles.

options.name: allowlegacykdf
options.description: FIPS 140-3 certification requires all handshakes without EMS be blocked.  Such KDFs are allowed by default. This setting is to allow/disallow such legacy KDFs  when needed. This setting applies to both frontend and backend SSL profiles.

options.name: allowunknownsni
options.description: Controls how the handshake is handled when the server name extension does not match any of the bound certificates. These checks are performed only if the session is SNI enabled (i.e. when profile bound to vserver has SNIEnable and Client Hello arrived with SNI extension). Available settings function as follows : C(ENABLED)   - handshakes with an unknown SNI are allowed to continue, if a default cert is bound. DISLABED  - handshakes with an unknown SNI are not allowed to continue.

options.name: alpnprotocol
options.description: Application protocol supported by the server and used in negotiation of the protocol with the client. Possible values are C(HTTP1.1), C(HTTP2) and C(NONE). Default value is C(NONE) which implies application protocol is not enabled hence remain unknown to the TLS layer. This parameter is relevant only if SSL connection is handled by the virtual server of the type SSL_TCP.

options.name: api_path
options.description: Base NITRO API path. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: ciphername
options.description: The cipher group/alias/individual cipher configuration

options.name: cipherpriority
options.description: cipher priority

options.name: cipherredirect
options.description: State of Cipher Redirect. If this parameter is set to C(ENABLED), you can configure an SSL virtual server or service to display meaningful error messages if the SSL handshake fails because of a cipher mismatch between the virtual server or service and the client. This parameter is not applicable when configuring a backend profile.

options.name: cipherurl
options.description: The redirect URL to be used with the Cipher Redirect feature.

options.name: cleartextport
options.description: Port on which clear-text data is sent by the appliance to the server. Do not specify this parameter for SSL offloading with end-to-end encryption.

options.name: clientauth
options.description: State of client authentication. In service-based SSL offload, the service terminates the SSL handshake if the SSL client does not provide a valid certificate. This parameter is not applicable when configuring a backend profile.

options.name: clientauthuseboundcachain
options.description: Certficates bound on the VIP are used for validating the client cert. Certficates came along with client cert are not used for validating the client cert

options.name: clientcert
options.description: The rule for client certificate requirement in client authentication.

options.name: commonname
options.description: Name to be checked against the CommonName (CN) field in the server certificate bound to the SSL server.

options.name: defaultsni
options.description: Default domain name supported by the SSL virtual server. The parameter is effective, when zero touch certificate management is active for the SSL virtual server i.e. no manual SNI cert or default server cert is bound to the v-server. For SSL transactions, when SNI is not presented by the client, server-certificate corresponding to the default SNI, if available in the cert-store, is selected else connection is terminated.

options.name: denysslreneg
options.description: Deny renegotiation in specified circumstances. Available settings function as follows: * C(NO) - Allow SSL renegotiation. * C(FRONTEND_CLIENT) - Deny secure and nonsecure SSL renegotiation initiated by the client. * C(FRONTEND_CLIENTSERVER) - Deny secure and nonsecure SSL renegotiation initiated by the client or the Citrix ADC during policy-based client authentication. * C(ALL) - Deny all secure and nonsecure SSL renegotiation. * C(NONSECURE) - Deny nonsecure SSL renegotiation. Allows only clien

options.name: dh
options.description: State of Diffie-Hellman (DH) key exchange. This parameter is not applicable when configuring a backend profile.

options.name: dhcount
options.description: Number of interactions, between the client and the Citrix ADC, after which the DH private-public pair is regenerated. A value of zero (0) specifies refresh every time. This parameter is not applicable when configuring a backend profile. Allowed DH count values are 0 and >= 500.

options.name: dhekeyexchangewithpsk
options.description: Whether or not the SSL Virtual Server will require a DHE key exchange to occur when a PSK is accepted during a TLS 1.3 resumption handshake. A DHE key exchange ensures forward secrecy even in the event that ticket keys are compromised, at the expense of an additional round trip and resources required to carry out the DHE key exchange. If disabled, a DHE key exchange will be performed when a PSK is accepted but only if requested by the client. If enabled, the server will require a DHE key exchang

options.name: dhfile
options.description: The file name and path for the DH parameter.

options.name: dhkeyexpsizelimit
options.description: This option enables the use of NIST recommended (NIST Special Publication 800-56A) bit size for private-key size. For example, for DH params of size 2048bit, the private-key size recommended is 224bits. This is rounded-up to 256bits.

options.name: dropreqwithnohostheader
options.description: Host header check for SNI enabled sessions. If this check is enabled and the HTTP request does not contain the host header for SNI enabled sessions(i.e vserver or profile bound to vserver has SNI enabled and 'Client Hello' arrived with SNI extension), the request is dropped.

options.name: encryptedclienthello
options.description: State of TLS 1.3 Encrypted Client Hello Support

options.name: encrypttriggerpktcount
options.description: Maximum number of queued packets after which encryption is triggered. Use this setting for SSL transactions that send small packets from server to Citrix ADC.

options.name: ersa
options.description: State of Ephemeral RSA (eRSA) key exchange. Ephemeral RSA allows clients that support only export ciphers to communicate with the secure server even if the server certificate does not support export clients. The ephemeral RSA key is automatically generated when you bind an export cipher to an SSL or TCP-based SSL virtual server or service. When you remove the export cipher, the eRSA key is not deleted. It is reused at a later date when another export cipher is bound to an SSL or TCP-based SSL vi

options.name: ersacount
options.description: The  refresh  count  for the re-generation of RSA public-key and private-key pair.

options.name: hsts
options.description: State of HSTS protocol support for the SSL profile. Using HSTS, a server can enforce the use of an HTTPS connection for all communication with a client

options.name: includesubdomains
options.description: Enable HSTS for subdomains. If set to Yes, a client must send only HTTPS requests for subdomains.

options.name: insertionencoding
options.description: Encoding method used to insert the subject or issuer's name in HTTP requests to servers.

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_id
options.description: The ID of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_ip
options.description: The IP of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_name
options.description: The name of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_password
options.description: The password of the managed NetScaler instance. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call In Settings > Administration > System Configurations > Basic Settings, if you select Prompt Credentials for Instance Login, ensure to configure username and password of a managed instance.

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_username
options.description: The username of the managed NetScaler instance. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call In Settings > Administration > System Configurations > Basic Settings, if you select Prompt Credentials for Instance Login, ensure to configure username and password of a managed instance.

options.name: maxage
options.description: Set the maximum time, in seconds, in the strict transport security (STS) header during which the client must send only HTTPS requests to the server

options.name: maxrenegrate
options.description: Maximum number of renegotiation requests allowed, in one second, to each SSL entity to which this profile is bound. When set to 0, an unlimited number of renegotiation requests are allowed. Applicable only when Deny SSL renegotiation is set to a value other than ALL.

options.name: name
options.description: Name for the SSL profile. Must begin with an ASCII alphanumeric or underscore (_) character, and must contain only ASCII alphanumeric, underscore, hash (#), period (.), space, colon (:), at (@), equals (=), and hyphen (-) characters. Cannot be changed after the profile is created.

options.name: netscaler_console_as_proxy_server
options.description: The IP address of the NetScaler ADC appliance acting as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: nitro_auth_token
options.description: The authentication token provided by a login operation.

options.name: nitro_pass
options.description: The password with which to authenticate to the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: nitro_protocol
options.description: Which protocol to use when accessing the nitro API objects.

options.name: nitro_user
options.description: The username with which to authenticate to the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: nsip
options.description: The ip address of the NetScaler ADC appliance where the nitro API calls will be made. The port can be specified with the colon (:). E.g. 192.168.1.1:555.

options.name: ocspstapling
options.description: State of OCSP stapling support on the SSL virtual server. Supported only if the protocol used is higher than SSLv3. Possible values: C(ENABLED): The appliance sends a request to the OCSP responder to check the status of the server certificate and caches the response for the specified time. If the response is valid at the time of SSL handshake with the client, the OCSP-based server certificate status is sent to the client during the handshake. C(DISABLED): The appliance does not check the status

options.name: preload
options.description: Flag indicates the consent of the site owner to have their domain preloaded.

options.name: prevsessionkeylifetime
options.description: This option sets the life time of symm key used to generate session tickets issued by NS in secs

options.name: pushenctrigger
options.description: Trigger encryption on the basis of the PUSH flag value. Available settings function as follows: * ALWAYS - Any PUSH packet triggers encryption. * IGNORE - C(Ignore) PUSH packet for triggering encryption. * MERGE - For a consecutive sequence of PUSH packets, the last PUSH packet triggers encryption. * TIMER - PUSH packet triggering encryption is delayed by the time defined in the set ssl parameter command or in the Change Advanced SSL Settings dialog box.

options.name: pushenctriggertimeout
options.description: PUSH encryption trigger timeout value. The timeout value is applied only if you set the Push Encryption Trigger parameter to Timer in the SSL virtual server settings.

options.name: pushflag
options.description: Insert PUSH flag into decrypted, encrypted, or all records. If the PUSH flag is set to a value other than 0, the buffered records are forwarded on the basis of the value of the PUSH flag. Available settings function as follows: 0 - Auto (PUSH flag is not set.) 1 - Insert PUSH flag into every decrypted record. 2 -Insert PUSH flag into every encrypted record. 3 - Insert PUSH flag into every decrypted and encrypted record.

options.name: quantumsize
options.description: Amount of data to collect before the data is pushed to the crypto hardware for encryption. For large downloads, a larger quantum size better utilizes the crypto resources.

options.name: redirectportrewrite
options.description: State of the port rewrite while performing HTTPS redirect. If this parameter is set to C(ENABLED), and the URL from the server does not contain the standard port, the port is rewritten to the standard.

options.name: remove_non_updatable_params
options.description: When given yes, the module will remove any parameters that are not updatable in the resource. If no, the module will return error if any non-updatable parameters are provided.

options.name: save_config
options.description: If C(true) the module will save the configuration on the NetScaler ADC node if it makes any changes. The module will not save the configuration on the NetScaler ADC node if it made no changes.

options.name: sendclosenotify
options.description: Enable sending SSL Close-Notify at the end of a transaction.

options.name: serverauth
options.description: State of server authentication support for the SSL Backend profile.

options.name: sessionkeylifetime
options.description: This option sets the life time of symm key used to generate session tickets issued by NS in secs

options.name: sessionticket
options.description: This option enables the use of session tickets, as per the RFC 5077

options.name: sessionticketkeydata
options.description: Session ticket enc/dec key , admin can set it

options.name: sessionticketkeyrefresh
options.description: This option enables the use of session tickets, as per the RFC 5077

options.name: sessionticketlifetime
options.description: This option sets the life time of session tickets issued by NS in secs

options.name: sessreuse
options.description: State of session reuse. Establishing the initial handshake requires CPU-intensive public key encryption operations. With the C(ENABLED) setting, session key exchange is avoided for session resumption requests received from the client.

options.name: sesstimeout
options.description: The Session timeout value in seconds.

options.name: skipclientcertpolicycheck
options.description: This flag controls the processing of X509 certificate policies. If this option is Enabled, then the policy check in Client authentication will be skipped. This option can be used only when Client Authentication is Enabled and ClientCert is set to Mandatory

options.name: snienable
options.description: State of the Server Name Indication (SNI) feature on the virtual server and service-based offload. SNI helps to enable SSL encryption on multiple domains on a single virtual server or service if the domains are controlled by the same organization and share the same second-level domain name. For example, *.sports.net can be used to secure domains such as login.sports.net and help.sports.net.

options.name: snihttphostmatch
options.description: Controls how the HTTP 'Host' header value is validated. These checks are performed only if the session is SNI enabled (i.e when vserver or profile bound to vserver has SNI enabled and 'Client Hello' arrived with SNI extension) and HTTP request contains 'Host' header. Available settings function as follows: C(CERT)   - Request is forwarded if the 'Host' value is covered          by the certificate used to establish this SSL session.          Note: 'C(CERT)' matching mode cannot be applied in

options.name: ssl3
options.description: State of SSLv3 protocol support for the SSL profile. Note: On platforms with SSL acceleration chips, if the SSL chip does not support SSLv3, this parameter cannot be set to C(ENABLED).

options.name: sslclientlogs
options.description: When enabled, NetScaler will log the session ID and SNI name during SSL handshakes on both the external and internal interfaces.

options.name: sslimaxsessperserver
options.description: Maximum ssl session to be cached per dynamic origin server. A unique ssl session is created for each SNI received from the client on ClientHello and the matching session is used for server session reuse.

options.name: sslinterception
options.description: Enable or disable transparent interception of SSL sessions.

options.name: ssliocspcheck
options.description: Enable or disable OCSP check for origin server certificate.

options.name: sslireneg
options.description: Enable or disable triggering the client renegotiation when renegotiation request is received from the origin server.

options.name: ssllogprofile
options.description: The name of the ssllogprofile.

options.name: sslprofile_ecccurve_binding
options.description: Bindings for sslprofile_ecccurve_binding resource

options.name: sslprofile_sslcertkey_binding
options.description: Bindings for sslprofile_sslcertkey_binding resource

options.name: sslprofile_sslcipher_binding
options.description: Bindings for sslprofile_sslcipher_binding resource

options.name: sslprofile_sslciphersuite_binding
options.description: Bindings for sslprofile_sslciphersuite_binding resource

options.name: sslprofile_sslechconfig_binding
options.description: Bindings for sslprofile_sslechconfig_binding resource

options.name: sslprofiletype
options.description: Type of profile. Front end profiles apply to the entity that receives requests from a client. Backend profiles apply to the entity that sends client requests to a server.

options.name: sslredirect
options.description: State of HTTPS redirects for the SSL service. For an SSL session, if the client browser receives a redirect message, the browser tries to connect to the new location. However, the secure SSL session breaks if the object has moved from a secure site (https://) to an unsecure site (http://). Typically, a warning message appears on the screen, prompting the user to continue or disconnect. If SSL Redirect is C(ENABLED), the redirect message is automatically converted from http:// to https:// and the

options.name: ssltriggertimeout
options.description: Time, in milliseconds, after which encryption is triggered for transactions that are not tracked on the Citrix ADC because their length is not known. There can be a delay of up to 10ms from the specified timeout value before the packet is pushed into the queue.

options.name: state
options.description: The state of the resource being configured by the module on the NetScaler ADC node. When C(present), the resource will be added/updated configured according to the module's parameters. When C(absent), the resource will be deleted from the NetScaler ADC node. When C(unset), the resource will be unset on the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: strictcachecks
options.description: Enable strict CA certificate checks on the appliance.

options.name: strictsigdigestcheck
options.description: Parameter indicating to check whether peer entity certificate during TLS1.2 handshake is signed with one of signature-hash combination supported by Citrix ADC.

options.name: tls1
options.description: State of TLSv1.0 protocol support for the SSL profile.

options.name: tls11
options.description: State of TLSv1.1 protocol support for the SSL profile.

options.name: tls12
options.description: State of TLSv1.2 protocol support for the SSL profile.

options.name: tls13
options.description: State of TLSv1.3 protocol support for the SSL profile.

options.name: tls13sessionticketsperauthcontext
options.description: Number of tickets the SSL Virtual Server will issue anytime TLS 1.3 is negotiated, ticket-based resumption is enabled, and either (1) a handshake completes or (2) post-handhsake client auth completes. This value can be increased to enable clients to open multiple parallel connections using a fresh ticket for each connection. No tickets are sent if resumption is disabled.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If C(false), SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only be used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.

options.name: zerorttearlydata
options.description: State of TLS 1.3 0-RTT early data support for the SSL Virtual Server. This setting only has an effect if resumption is enabled, as early data cannot be sent along with an initial handshake. Early application data has significantly different security properties - in particular there is no guarantee that the data cannot be replayed.
